plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: Cascading chains of fragrant, pea-like flowers drape from twining woody vines. They turn pergolas, walls and old trees into curtains of lilac-purple. The scent is sweet and grape-like, and it draws bumblebees in large numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring, typically April to early May in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Native to China and widely grown in gardens across Europe, Japan and the eastern United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine counterclockwise, and a mature plant can live for well over a century. Some vines grow strong enough to crush the structures that support them.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms stand on smooth, upright stems above blue-green leaves. Their colors range from clear primary shades to feathered and fringed forms. Late-season varieties keep Northern Hemisphere borders bright into May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, with late-flowering types peaking late April through mid-May
plants.location: Gardens across the Netherlands, the Pacific Northwest and the northeastern United States, and northern Europe
plants.funFact: During 1630s Dutch 'tulip mania', single bulbs sold for more than the price of a canal house.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: Drooping, bell-shaped flowers hang from one side of arching stems. They carpet ancient woodland floors in a hazy blue sheet. The sweet scent drifts through the trees in the dappled light.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to late May, usually peaking around early May
plants.location: Ancient woodlands of the United Kingdom, Ireland and western Europe
plants.funFact: The United Kingdom holds about half of the world's bluebell population, and the plant is legally protected there against being dug up from the wild.
